title: Week 2 of building a 3D threejs world for an Elder Scrolls spinoff
author: Potential_Ad_7544
selftext:
This project is about creating a standlone, browser-based, Threejs Elder Scrolls spinoff. What I want to do is create something that has:

* The soul of Morrowind
* The combat of dark souls 1
* Set in Argonia (the Black Marsh)
* An all-new set of quests, locations, NPCs, all the rest of it
* Approximately Skyrim level (2011) graphics, for achievability

I have literally been dreaming of being able to play something like that since I was a 10 year old kid in the early noughties (and then again in the 2010s after playing dark souls for the first time). There have been various attempts at doing something like it as mods for Morrowind/Oblivio/Skyrim and none have quite delivered what I want to date. So I thought, hey, let's give it a go, maybe I can make my childhood dream come true.

I've never done anything with modding before and wanted to have full control over the engine in ways that I don't know would be achievable by building a more traditional mod for e.g. Skyrim. (A lot of what made me sad about the TES games post Morrowind was that they cut a lot of the soul that everyone loved from it and I've not seen any mods that successfully restore it, to my knowledge).

Secondary goal was also to create a bunch of reusable threejs stuff that other people in this community may be able to pick up and create with, shortcutting a bunch of the hassle that you have to go through to get something half usable with claude. If there is interest from people here I will happily open source this - is this something people would be keen for?

What we have after 2 weeks:

* **Terrain**, based on the [All Tamriel Heightmap project](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/573) and then heavily modified between me and claude - adding erosion-simulation based mountains, watersheds, converting coarse contours to smooth them out, adding hydrology and a bunch of other stuff. Even though the base is a heightmap somebody made for Tamriel, in theory you should be able to point your coding agent at the repo I'm making and ask it to adapt to any other setting/geography of your choice
* **Water** \- which as many of you will know is a *massive pain in the arse*. Mine doesn't really work yet. It's attempted to be based on WaterThreeJs and [threejs-water](https://github.com/jeantimex/threejs-water) and some other things. It's kind of a placeholder for now - if anyone has any advice I would hugely welcome it.
* **Natural light** \- surprised me how challenging this was to get the feel of it reasonably OK, again hopefully should be easily reusable
* **Day and night cycle**, moon phases
* **Weather**, mist, haze, clouds, rain, realistic interaction between sunlight/moonlight and weather; varying conditions within and between days and seasons; morning mist burning off in the afternoon, etc
* **Seasons** \- wet season, dry season, daily tides, stormier seas in rougher weather; Tamriel calendar
* **Basic physics** \- controlling the character, walking, running, jumping, interacting with water (buggily), colliding with terrain, etc

Things that also are hard and that I'm not really trying to tackle here:

* **Creating assets** \- as it's an Elder Scrolls spinoff I'm using character/vegetation/item etc meshes and animations directly from Skyrim and from mods. Frankly having a go at this has made me start to appreciate the truly vast scale of asset work you would need if you were making an original game of this type. There are lots of good workflows documented elsewhere in this community though if you do plan to give it a go. 
* **Textures** \- related to above - I'm using some CC0 textures and some from Skyrim/mods. If you were adapting this world you could get your agent to research open source ones and/or create new ones. Again, doing it made me start to appreciate that you probably need way more of them than you think.
* **Gameplay systems** \- have a bit of a plan for what to build out if and when I can make a world that feels worth playing in (and have done some combat sandbox stuff already). Again as it's an Elder Souls spinoff I'm essentially planning to implement lots of the systems from Morrowind, merged with some stuff from Dark Souls and Skyrim (and probably some breath of the wild style climbing), tweaked for taste. Using Rapier physics and [ecctrl](https://github.com/pmndrs/ecctrl) for the 3d player controller and for full control over the engine. Recurring theme - starting to dig into this again made me appreciate massively (a) just *how many* interacting systems go into a big RPG, even one that's 24 years old like Morrowind, and any one of which can accidentally break a load of the others; and (b) what a daunting task it would be to create an actually 'fun' set of systems from scratch. Even just using AI to repurpose and combine systems that teams of humans have already spent years making good - is looking surprisingly daunting. Coming up with that stuff from scratch for a new game is... a big task. Whenever Fable has made suggestions on gameplay systems so far for even just this project, they have often either clearly been destined for failure (over-ambitious or clearly would break something else if implemented) or just felt a bit "off". So I'm not convinced even the best models can currently by themselves design a good set of big interacting systems for a good game, and you're going to be doing a lot of guiding if you want to try (which tbh also for me is the fun part).

  
Anyway unnecessarily long post but happy to answer questions; keen to know if anyone would find it useful if I open sourced the repo; and good luck to all of you on your gamedev adventures.

comments.author: Quiet-Phase6948
comments.body: Three.js is garbage for these type of things, so why are you using it?

replies.author: Potential_Ad_7544
replies.body: Probably inexperience to be honest - I'm new to all of this. 10+ years coding in other professional contexts but never game dev by hand (some web dev which probably is behind instinctively gravitating towards browser and js). What would you recommend instead? I also considered unity and godot. For various reasons am constrained to running on a Linux VM Vs code cloud instance that I can't easily install other desktop software on (have been using headless blender on there via CLI though) so that restricts somewhat. Tbh also was just interested to see how far you can go with js. But if there are better approaches would very much welcome the advice

replies.author: ReindeerOk2009
replies.body: It’s not garbage for open world. It carries some platform tax but you’re getting it in web browser.
